description:
Why N-able:

At N-able, we’re not just helping businesses be secure —we’re redefining what it means to be cyber resilient. Our end-to-end platform blends AI-powered capabilities and flexible tech stacks, so customers can manage, secure, and recover with confidence. But the real power behind it all? Our people. We’re a global crew of N-ablites, who love solving complex problems, sharing knowledge, and delivering solutions that actually make a difference. If you're into meaningful work, fast growth, and a team that’s got your back, you’ll be surrounded by people who believe in what they do—and in you.

What You'll Do:

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own a defined area spanning network discovery and asset monitoring, including its roadmap and delivery. Network discovery is about finding and mapping the devices and assets in a customer's environment. Asset monitoring covers monitoring for security, device health, and device observability. The two connect closely, since you can only monitor what you can see, but each is an area in its own right with its own problems, users, and roadmap. You'll work with the guidance of a Principal PM or product leadership on strategy, and you'll be trusted to run day-to-day execution on your own.

N-able PMs are full-stack PMs. You'll partner closely with engineering on what gets built and why, but the job doesn't stop at the backlog. You're expected to understand how MSPs operate, how customer environments are built and monitored, the competitive landscape, and where the technology is heading, and to bring that into decisions others can act on. You'll regularly be in front of partners and customers.

Product areas at N-able are flexible. As priorities and the market evolve, the areas our PMs own can change, and your focus may shift or broaden over time. We're looking for someone who sees that as an opportunity to grow.

  

* Own the roadmap and delivery for your area across network discovery and asset monitoring, contributing to its strategy and covering the lifecycle from discovery to launch.
* Translate MSP problems around device discovery, network visibility, security monitoring of assets, device health, observability, alerting, and noise reduction into clear product requirements, epics, and user stories, and explain the tradeoffs behind them.
* Make sure what gets discovered feeds what gets monitored, so that discovery and monitoring work as a coherent experience for the technician while each keeps its own roadmap.
* Partner day to day with engineering and architecture to deliver capabilities that measurably improve discovery coverage, monitoring coverage and accuracy, time to detect device issues, time to onboard, and technician efficiency.
* Run continuous discovery with MSP partners, internal IT teams, and prospects, separating what people ask for from what they actually need.
* Track the competitive landscape (RMM, network discovery and monitoring, asset monitoring, observability, ITOM) for your area and feed it into positioning and roadmap decisions.
* Build reliability, scalability, security, performance, and ease of use into product design, particularly for monitoring at scale across many customer environments.
* Define and track success metrics for your area, such as adoption, retention, and monitoring coverage, and act when they move the wrong way.
* Work with product marketing, sales, and support on launches, enablement, webinars, and analyst or customer briefings.
* Take on new or changing product areas as priorities shift, bringing your learning and good practice with you.
* Support and informally mentor newer product managers, sharing good practice with the team.

What You'll Bring:

* 7+ years in product management, including at least 2 years on SaaS products in IT management, network management, monitoring, or related infrastructure domains.
* Technical background in IT infrastructure, endpoint, and network management technologies, and a strong understanding of how MSPs manage IT for their customers.
* Self-motivation and comfort with ambiguity and change. You can take a loosely defined problem, make decisions, communicate them, and follow through with moderate supervision, and you adapt well when your area of focus shifts.
* Strong product sense: good instincts for what to build, what to cut, and what "good" looks like for a technician managing many customer environments under time pressure.
* A track record of shipping SaaS products in an Agile/Scrum environment.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and clear, professional communication with customers and internal stakeholders.
* Bachelor's degree; a Master's degree is preferred.

At CommBank, you will work in an environment that aims to combine the scale and responsibility of Australia's leading bank with empowered, product-led teams. It also means delivering safely and sustainably: risk, resilience and controls are part of good product design, not something added at the end. We value people who demonstrate Care, Courage and Commitment. You will have the opportunity to work on a material payments problem, own an important product area within a new strategic capability, collaborate with deep payments and technology specialists, and explore how automation and emerging AI can responsibly transform payment servicing.

**Location:** Bangalore

**Business & Team:**

As Product Lead - Payment Exceptions & Investigations, you will own a defined product area within the broader Payment Exceptions & Investigations product stream. Working within the product strategy and direction established for the stream, you will translate customer and operational problems into clear product outcomes, priorities and an executable roadmap for your squad. You will lead the product lifecycle for your area from discovery and problem definition through delivery, adoption, run performance and continuous optimisation. You will make evidence-based trade-offs across customer value, operational efficiency, risk, technology and delivery considerations, partnering closely with Engineering, Design, Architecture, Payments Operations, frontline teams, Risk and other specialist teams.

You will work closely with other Product Leads and Product Managers across the PEX stream to ensure your product area contributes to coherent end-to-end payment exception journeys and reusable capabilities rather than creating isolated solutions.

You will be responsible for developing and delivering customer reporting capability for the Payments Domain. **Team Overview**

The Product TPM team operates at the intersection of business, technology, and delivery, enabling the successful development and rollout of scalable, customer-centric solutions. At the Consultant (P03) level, the team is composed of Technical Product Managers who own feature-level delivery while collaborating closely with engineering, design, and business stakeholders.
  
The team functions within an Agile framework, ensuring continuous delivery of high-quality product increments through iterative development, sprint cycles, and regular feedback loops. Each TPM is responsible for managing specific product modules or features, contributing to the broader product roadmap while aligning execution with organizational goals and customer needs.

This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.  
  

**Role Overview And Core Responsibilities**

The Consultant (P03) – Technical Product Management (TPM) role is responsible for driving the end-to-end delivery of technology-enabled product features by effectively bridging business requirements with engineering execution. The role combines product ownership, technical understanding, and Agile delivery to ensure the development of scalable, high-quality solutions aligned with customer needs and organizational priorities.

At this level, the TPM owns feature-level execution, collaborates closely with cross-functional teams, and contributes to product strategy and roadmap under guidance from senior product leaders.
  
  
Role Overview And Core Responsibilities

**1. Product Ownership**

* Own and manage assigned product features or modules from concept to delivery
* Define detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, and maintain the product backlog
* Prioritize deliverables based on business value, customer impact, and feasibility

**2. Product Strategy & Roadmap Support**

* Contribute to product roadmap planning and execution
* Align feature development with overall product vision and business objectives
* Incorporate stakeholder input, user feedback, and analytics insights

**3. Technical Collaboration**

* Translate business requirements into clear technical specifications
* Work closely with engineering teams on solution design and implementation
* Assess technical trade-offs, dependencies, and constraints
* Ensure adherence to scalability, security, and performance standards

**4. Agile Delivery Execution**

* Actively participate in Agile ceremonies (sprint planning, grooming, stand-ups, retrospectives)
* Ensure timely and high-quality delivery of product increments
* Support continuous improvement in development and delivery processes

**5. Stakeholder Management**

* Collaborate with business, engineering, and UX/design teams
* Act as the primary point of contact for owned features
* Communicate progress, risks, and outcomes effectively

**6. Data-Driven Decision Making**

* Define and track KPIs for product features
* Use product analytics and user insights to drive improvements
* Optimize product performance, usability, and adoption

**7. Product Lifecycle Support**

* Support the full product lifecycle including requirement gathering, development, testing, and release
* Assist in documentation, training, and user adoption initiatives

Ensure smooth rollout and continuous enhancement of features

  

**Required Knowledge And Experiences**

The ideal candidate should have 5–8 years of experience in Technical Product Management, Product Management, or software/program delivery roles, with a strong understanding of the product lifecycle and Agile methodologies. They should possess solid knowledge of SDLC, ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications, and familiarity with tools like Jira and Confluence. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills are essential, along with the ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams. A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field is required, with Agile certifications (CSPO/CSM) considered an added advantage.
